The 2006-2015 version asked how many of the last 14 days the respondent felt down, depressed or hopeless, while the 2018 version uses four frequency categories (Never to Nearly every day), so the response scales cannot be pooled.

Question and answers are identical in 2005 and 2007 ('During the past 30 days, how many days did you take a prescription asthma medication to PREVENT an asthma attack from occurring?'); only the dataset label changed from TIMES to DAYS.

The question is the same in both years, asking how many drinks the respondent drank on the average on the days when they drank; the 2005 revision only added an explicit drink-size definition and made the past 30 days timeframe explicit. AVEDRNK3 added code 88 for None, which AVEDRNK2 did not use, so a report of no drinks is coded differently in the two generations.
Codes and answer labels are identical across the rename; the 2024 rename accompanied _DRNKWK2 to _DRNKWK3, where the question stem and the calculation are unchanged.

Both compute the same body mass index and at the 1999 to 2000 boundary both store one implied decimal (about 25.6 stored as 256), but from 2001 _BMI2 switches to more decimal places, so check the stored scale before pooling.
Same body mass index on the same stored scale (two implied decimals) on both sides of the rename.
The BMI definition and stored scale are unchanged; 2004 began letting respondents report height and weight in metric units, which feeds the same calculation.
Same computed body mass index on the same stored scale; the rename tracks the 2011 survey redesign, which changed weighting rather than the definition.

Wording is identical in 2000 and 2001 ('Have you ever been told by a doctor, nurse, or other health professional that you have high blood pressure?'); the item moved from an optional module into the core.

Wording is identical at the rename ('Are you currently taking prescription medicine for your high blood pressure?' in both 2021 and 2023); the word 'prescription' was added around 2019 while the variable was still named BPMEDS.
Codes and answer labels are identical apart from the apostrophe in the don't-know label; question wording not independently confirmed.

The BRTHCNT name was reused in 2022 for a different question. In the 2022 module the yes-or-no question is the separate variable PFPPRVN4 and the first-method question is TYPCNTR9.

The 1997 item was fixed core question 77c in the HIV/AIDS section, asked only of respondents who said they had changed their sexual behavior because of HIV in the past 12 months, and it asked whether one of the changes they made was to now always use condoms for protection. Response codes were yes, no, don't know, and refused.

The 1998 optional Sexual Behavior module kept the changed-behavior gate but reworded the item from a report of a change made in the past 12 months to the current status question of whether the respondent now always uses condoms for protection, and it added a not applicable response code that took about 8 percent of asked respondents in 1998. The question wording and code set stayed identical through 2001, although the 2001 administration restricted the module to respondents aged 49 or younger and coded abstinent respondents as not applicable, which raised that code to about 44 percent of asked respondents. The change-report versus current-status framing and the new response code make estimates not comparable with the 1997 fixed core item.
